Clarity.justification: The paper is well-structured with clear sections on introduction, related work, method, experiments, and results. Mathematical formulations for Marchenko-Pastur bulk edge and alignment metric A(θ) are explicitly defined. Tables and figures are referenced appropriately. Minor issues include buried discussion of incomplete experiments (e.g., H-M2 untested due to random basis) and limited detail on why 5-epoch interpolation paths were used.

Novelty.justification: The work applies Marchenko-Pastur random matrix theory (previously used by Sagun et al. 2017 for Hessian spectra) to distinguish spurious correlation exploitation via curvature subspace alignment on Waterbirds. This is an incremental extension rather than a groundbreaking idea; no new theoretical framework or multi-dataset benchmarks are introduced.

Soundness.justification: Primary results rely on a single random seed. Two of four mechanism hypotheses fail (H-M2 untested with random basis yielding ~0 alignment; H-M4 refuted with ρ=0.045, p=0.85). Interpolation experiments use only 5 epochs, producing endpoint WGA of 32.3%/9.8% instead of expected 72%/88%. Code logs confirm failures (e.g., 'No significant negative correlation found', dataset download errors, CUDA OOM). Results are not shown to be reliable or consistent with full training protocols.

Significance.justification: Addresses an important problem but is limited to Waterbirds with no generalization to CelebA/Colored MNIST or other modalities. The geometric signature distinguishes regimes but shows no predictive power for robustness without group labels. No lasting impact is demonstrated due to incomplete mechanisms and single-dataset scope.

strengths: Clear exposition of Marchenko-Pastur application to Hessian outlier detection
Explicit reporting of failed hypotheses and limitations
weaknesses: Single-seed primary experiment and incomplete mechanism validation
Path experiments use severely under-trained models, invalidating coupling conclusions
